page: Microsoft Azure D64ds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Ddsv7 family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C x86_64 processor with 64 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz and features a large 480 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance includes 3780 GB of local disk capacity and supports Premium Storage. No GPUs are included in this configuration.

In benchmark evaluations, the D64ds_v7 demonstrates strong multi-core capabilities, achieving a top-tier PassMark CPU score in the top 10% and a strong stress-ng multi-core CPU performance rating in the top 25%. Single-core performance is moderate, falling in the middle 50% range. Memory subsystem performance is robust, with uncached large-block read bandwidth reaching 326.02 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 127.56 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25%. The processor's support for Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) accelerates specialized mathematical computations, as evidenced by top-tier prompt processing speeds of 3946.15 tokens/sec for small LLM inference models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D64ds_v7 offers high resource density by combining a high-frequency 64-vCPU compute profile with a substantial 3780 GB local storage allocation, reducing the need for external storage attachments for data-intensive tasks. This hardware profile is highly suited for enterprise database operations, high-throughput static web serving, multi-threaded decompression tasks, and small-scale language model inference.

It is highly suited for database operations, multi-threaded data decompression, static web serving, and small-scale LLM inference.
